findings.current: Even a well-known court official couldn’t enter or leave without an authorized pass.
findings.defect: The source specifies an official whose face was known. “Well-known court official” can instead imply that the official was prominent or widely reputed, losing the point that recognition by face did not grant access.
findings.rationale: The Korean says 얼굴이 알려진 조정의 관리—literally, a court official whose face was known—and contrasts that recognition with the requirement for an authorized pass.
findings.replacement: Even a court official whose face was well known couldn’t enter or leave without an authorized pass.

summary: The assembled translation is faithful overall, with one minor loss of precision about how recognizable a court official would be.
